skill.name: Fact or opinion
skill.why: Persuaders mix facts and opinions. Knowing which is which stops you being fooled.
skill.how: Ask: could I check this and prove it true or false? Yes means fact claim.

beats.say: A fact is something you could check.
Look at the scoreboard. It's either true or false.
An opinion is what someone thinks. You can't prove it.
beats.show: The Reef Rays are **the best team ever**.

beats.say: Watch for words like best, boring and should.
Careful! A fact can be checked, even when it's wrong.
beats.show: Maxx: '**I have rescued 500 Creatures.**' False, but you can check it. Fact.

encounters.text: Dear Editor, I am writing about the oval at Red Dune Park, where the Bluster Rock Roos play their home games. The oval has no lights. Last season, four games were cancelled because it got too dark to see the ball. Our under-12s now train at 4 pm, which means half the team misses training because of after-school jobs and buses. The council has ignored footy fans for far too long. Night games under lights are twice as exciting as day games, and they would bring crowds back to the club. Lights for the oval would cost about $80,000. The council should pay the $80,000 by next winter. Our kids deserve a proper place to play. Last month, more than three hundred people signed a petition asking for lights. Other towns nearby, like Saltbush Creek, put lights on their ovals years ago, and their junior teams have doubled in size. Please, council, do the right thing. Yours sincerely, Dev Marsh, coach of the Bluster Rock Roos

encounters.frame: A furious letter in the Bluster Rock Bugle. The Proovil is reading it from inside a rock pool.
encounters.text: Dear Editor, I am writing to object to the council's decision to allow jet ski hire in Bluster Bay. For decades, the northern end of the bay has been a nesting beach for green turtles, and every summer, volunteers count the nests and fence them off. Since the hire shop opened in October, rangers have counted fourteen injured turtles, most with cuts on their shells that match the shape of a propeller. The hire shop is owned by a company called Gold Rush Rentals, which also sponsors Maxx Vantablack's channel. Each nest holds around a hundred eggs, and only a tiny number of hatchlings ever survive to become adults. When I raised this at the last council meeting, I was told the hire shop brings 'valuable tourism' to the town. A bay with fourteen injured turtles is no place for jet skis. The council's October decision was reckless and short-sighted, and it was made without asking a single local. Surely nobody wants to see a turtle hurt for the sake of a joyride. Bluster Bay is far too precious to be ruined by noisy machines. I urge every reader to come to the council meeting on 12 December and make their voice heard. Yours faithfully, Ada Pennick, turtle volunteer

encounters.frame: Maxx is auctioning a painting on his stream. The Proovil's spikes have never stood so straight.
encounters.text: Maxx it out, Vantafam! Tonight, I am auctioning one of my own paintings, and every cent goes to the Maxx Vantablack Rescue Fund. It's called 'Gold on Gold', and I painted it myself in under ten minutes, using a brush made from my own hair. The canvas measures two metres across, and it's covered in real gold paint. Honestly, it is a masterpiece. Its bold colours capture the spirit of the outback in a way that no other painting ever has. Last year, my painting 'Me, Again' was the most expensive item sold at the Bluster Rock Art Auction, and that one only had silver. Before you ask, Vantafam, yes, I painted the frame as well. I've been painting since I was six, when I painted my first portrait, which was of me. This one only took ten minutes because genius doesn't need longer. Remember, every cent goes to rescuing Creatures, so you're basically a hero if you bid. No serious collector can afford to miss this. Bidding starts at $10,000, and it closes at midnight. Bids go in the comments, and my Goldies will read every single one aloud. If two people bid the same amount, the person with the nicer comment about my hair wins. That's Maxx-imum content! Stay gold!

encounters.frame: Gus has written up his science fair project. His summary has an opinion tucked inside.
encounters.text: SCIENCE FAIR REPORT: Which food grows mould fastest? by Gus. I left five foods in sealed jars on the windowsill of the Soggy Biscuit's galley for fourteen days: white bread, an orange, cheese, a boiled potato and one of Mo's fish-finger custards. I photographed each jar at the same time every morning and measured how much of the surface was covered in mould. Before starting, I predicted that the cheese would grow mould first, because it already smells like feet. The bread was the first to grow mould, with fluffy green spots appearing on day three. By day ten, the orange was completely covered in a blue-green fuzz. The cheese grew the least mould of the real foods. Mo's custard grew no mould at all, which I find deeply worrying. The potato grew a small patch of white mould on day seven, which Wren said looked like a tiny snowfield. Next time, I would like to test whether mould grows faster in the dark. In my opinion, mould is the most fascinating life form on the planet, and every school should have a mould garden. The smell in the galley on day fourteen was so strong that Tully moved her hammock onto the deck.

encounters.frame: Slick Vinnie is selling something new. The Proovil is not buying it.
encounters.text: LADIES, GENTLEMEN AND LIZARDS! Slick Vinnie proudly presents the Snore-Stopper 5000, a pillow that gently vibrates whenever the person sleeping on it begins to snore. Inside each pillow is a tiny microphone that switches on at 10 pm and off again at 6 am. The pillow comes in three colours: desert red, sky blue and galah pink. In a trial run by Vinnie's own family, his uncle Barry snored forty fewer times on the first night. The pillow is filled with recycled foam and can be washed in a normal washing machine, as long as you remove the microphone first. Vinnie has sold 120 pillows since Monday, mostly to people who live with uncles. Each one is guaranteed for two years. At just $49, the Snore-Stopper is frankly the most important invention since the wheel. Anyone who shares a room with a snorer would be mad not to buy one immediately. The Snore-Stopper costs $49, and each one comes with a free pair of earplugs, just in case. Order before Sunday and Vinnie will throw in a second pillowcase for free. Vinnie's aunty says the pillow has saved her marriage, although Uncle Barry says it keeps waking him up to tell him he's snoring.
